concepts.why: The patient has a hyperostotic lesion of the outer table of the right calvarium and a densely calcified mass involving the inferior squamosal portion of the right temporal bone, which is consistent with an osteoma.

The patient has pain and swelling in the right mastoid area, a small amount of fluid in the right mastoid air cells, and mucosal thickening in the right ethmoid air cells, which are consistent with mastoiditis.
The patient has a densely calcified mass with low signal intensity on T1- and T2-weighted images and mild patchy internal enhancement, which is consistent with a chondroma.

The patient has a hyperostotic lesion of the outer table of the right calvarium and a densely calcified mass involving the inferior squamosal portion of the right temporal bone, which is consistent with an osteochondroma.
The patient has a densely calcified mass with low signal intensity on T1- and T2-weighted images and mild patchy internal enhancement, which is consistent with eosinophilic granuloma.

The patient has pain and swelling in the right mastoid area, a small amount of fluid in the right mastoid air cells, and mucosal thickening in the right ethmoid air cells, which are consistent with chronic osteomyelitis.

The patient has a hyperostotic lesion of the outer table of the right calvarium and a densely calcified mass involving the inferior squamosal portion of the right temporal bone, which is consistent with fibrous dysplasia.
The patient has a densely calcified mass with low signal intensity on T1- and T2-weighted images and mild patchy internal enhancement, which is consistent with a giant cell tumor.
It explains the hyperostotic lesion of the outer table of the right calvarium without intracranial extension or adjacent soft-tissue mass.
